observed_shipment.requires: dated actual shipment/delivery evidence; explicit origin and destination scope
observed_shipment.geographic_arc: only with evidence for both endpoints; transport itinerary remains unknown unless sourced

trade_aggregate.requires: reporter/partner/product code/period/unit; countries or regions, not factories
trade_aggregate.mass_balance_default: only within exact matching trade boundary

company_contract.requires: named counterparties and dated contract/order; planned deliveries labelled

historical_relationship.requires: historical dated report; do not infer present continuity

product_adoption.requires: end product contains/uses company materials; direct procurement unproven

scenario_route.requires: scenario ID and explicit assumptions separate from observed graph

sector_application.requires: application/function evidence; denotes use class, not shipping route

guards: A factory pin establishes location/capability only, not a material route.
ABB Fort Smith motor evidence and ABB Shanghai robot capability do not establish a China→U.S. route.
Contracts at company scope must target company or anonymous-recipient nodes when receiving plant is unverified.
A component factory can connect to a sector and an end-product factory with different edge types; neither implies the magnet is manufactured there.
Shipping-country origin is not the original mine provenance. Imported intermediate origin and oxide/metal converter may differ.
Element filters denote supported product/assay evidence, not a guarantee all delivered grades contain every element.
No allocation percentage without an explicit same-boundary denominator; unknown fraction stays null. If denominator is known but allocation coverage is incomplete, display residual unallocated once.
Do not turn planned or anonymous qualification deliveries into series shipments to a named OEM.

example_edges.to_scope: unnamed Tier 1 traction-motor customer; site/country unknown
